title: Deriving the ordinary singleton extension
statement:
The ordinary singleton extension sends quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term independently K-flat B_n-complexes to quasi-isomorphisms of strict systems. It therefore admits normalized universal and pointwise derived left extension data, retaining its ordinary functor and adjunction exactly, computing on those complexes and left adjoint to actual derived evaluation.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J)) (T : SystemTensorCoherence S)
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (n : ℕ)
def systemSingleDerivedExtension (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J))
    (T : SystemTensorCoherence S) :
    SystemDerivedLeftExtension (systemEvaluation B n) (systemLevelKFlat B n)
```

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21, ordinary evaluation left extension and the subsequence generalization; Stacks 0FND, 09T5 and 015F

proof.text: Below n, the ordinary tensor comparison identifies each map with a scalar extension of a quasi-isomorphism between independent K-flat complexes; above n it is a map between zero complexes. Scalar change of rings preserves the former quasi-isomorphisms and the latter are automatic. Componentwise detection proves the system quasi-isomorphism. The independent-coefficient flat-term K-flat resolution theorem gives the resolving class, and the generic normalized left-extension construction applies.
